arxiv-2101-02555.title: Explainable AI and Adoption of Financial Algorithmic Advisors: an Experimental Study Conference: Proceedings of the 2021 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society; May 19–21, 2021; Virtual Event, USA Proceedings of the 2021 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES ’21), May 19–21, 2
arxiv-2101-02555.creator: Daniel Ben David, Yehezkel S. Resheff, Talia Tron
arxiv-2101-02555.description: Abstract . We study whether receiving advice from either a human or algorithmic advisor, accompanied by five types of Local and Global explanation labelings, has an effect on the readiness to adopt, willingness to pay, and trust in a financial AI consultant.

arxiv-2104-01973.title: Dynamical systems on hypergraphs
arxiv-2104-01973.creator: Timoteo Carletti and Duccio Fanelli
arxiv-2104-01973.description: Abstract We present a general framework that enables one to model high-order interaction among entangled dynamical systems, via hypergraphs. Several relevant processes can be ideally traced back to the proposed scheme. We shall here solely elaborate on the conditions that seed the spontaneous emergence of patterns, spatially heterogeneous solutions resulting from the many-body interaction between fundamental units.

arxiv-2111-14007.title: An Entropy Weighted Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Algorithm for Feature Representation
arxiv-2111-14007.creator: Jiao Wei, Can Tong, Bingxue Wu, Qiang He, Shouliang Qi, Yudong Yao, Yueyang Teng *
arxiv-2111-14007.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jiao Wei, Can Tong, Bingxue Wu, Qiang He, Shouliang Qi, Yudong Yao, Yueyang Teng *. Nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) has been widely used to learn low-dimensional representations of data. However, NMF pays the same attention to all attributes of a data point, which inevitably leads to inaccurate representation. For example, in a human-face data set, if an image contains a hat on the head, the hat should be removed or the importance of its corresponding attributes should be decreased during matrix factorizing.

arxiv-2210-03386.title: One-electron self-interaction error and its relationship to geometry and higher orbital occupation
arxiv-2210-03386.creator: Dale R. Lonsdale, Lars Goerigk
arxiv-2210-03386.description: Abstract Density Functional Theory (DFT) sees prominent use in computational chemistry and physics, however, problems due to the self-interaction error (SIE) pose additional challenges to obtaining qualitatively correct results. An unphysical energy an electron exerts on itself, the SIE impacts most practical DFT calculations.

arxiv-2309-16387.title: Streaming quantum state purification
arxiv-2309-16387.creator: Andrew M. Childs, Honghao Fu, Debbie Leung, Zhi Li, Maris Ozols, Vedang Vyas
arxiv-2309-16387.description: Abstract Quantum state purification is the task of recovering a nearly pure copy of an unknown pure quantum state using multiple noisy copies of the state. This basic task has applications to quantum communication over noisy channels and quantum computation with imperfect devices, but has primarily been studied previously for the case of qubits.

arxiv-2404-15454.title: Prediction from compression for models with infinite memory, with applications to hidden Markov and renewal processes
arxiv-2404-15454.creator: Yanjun Han, Tianze Jiang, Yihong Wu
arxiv-2404-15454.description: Abstract Consider the problem of predicting the next symbol given a sample path of length n n , whose joint distribution belongs to a distribution class that may have long-term memory. The goal is to compete with the conditional predictor that knows the true model.

arxiv-2411-08227.title: DPU: Dynamic Prototype Updating for Multimodal Out-of-Distribution Detection
arxiv-2411-08227.creator: Shawn Li, Huixian Gong, Hao Dong, Tiankai Yang, Zhengzhong Tu, Yue Zhao
arxiv-2411-08227.description: Abstract Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is crucial for ensuring the robustness of machine learning models by identifying samples that deviate from the training distribution. While traditional OOD detection has predominantly focused on single-modality inputs, such as images, recent advancements in multimodal models have shown the potential of utilizing multiple modalities (e.g., video, optical flow, audio) to improve detection performance.

arxiv-2411-13685.title: Using AI Large Language Models for Grading in Education: A Hands-On Test for Physics
arxiv-2411-13685.creator: Ryan Mok, Faraaz Akhtar, Louis Clare, Christine Li, Jun Ida, Lewis Ross, Mario Campanelli
arxiv-2411-13685.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ryan Mok, Faraaz Akhtar, Louis Clare, Christine Li, Jun Ida, Lewis Ross, Mario Campanelli. Grading assessments is time-consuming and prone to human bias. Students may experience delays in receiving feedback that may not be tailored to their expectations or needs. Harnessing AI in education can be effective for grading undergraduate physics problems, enhancing the efficiency of undergraduate-level physics learning and teaching, and helping students understand concepts with the help of a constantly available tutor.

arxiv-2504-15877.title: Universal transparency and fine band structure near the Dirac point in HgTe quantum wells
arxiv-2504-15877.creator: V. Dziom, A. Shuvaev, J. Gospodarič, E. G. Novik, A. A. Dobretsova, N. N. Mikhailov, Z. D. Kvon, Z. Alpichshev, A. Pimenov
arxiv-2504-15877.description: Abstract Spin–orbit coupling in thin HgTe quantum wells results in a relativistic-like electron band structure, making it a versatile solid state platform to observe and control non-trivial electrodynamic phenomena. Here we report an observation of universal terahertz (THz) transparency determined by fine-structure constant α ≈ 1 / 137 \alpha\approx 1/137 in 6.

arxiv-2507-09185.title: Detecting and Pruning Prominent but Detrimental Neurons in Large Language Models
arxiv-2507-09185.creator: Ameen Ali, Shahar Katz, Lior Wolf, Ivan Titov
arxiv-2507-09185.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) often develop learned mechanisms specialized to specific datasets, such as reliance on domain-specific correlations, which yield high-confidence predictions without generalizable reasoning. While beneficial in one setting, these dataset-specific mechanisms typically degrade performance when models encounter novel tasks or distributions.

arxiv-2508-07805.title: Can You Trick the Grader? Adversarial Persuasion of LLM Judges
arxiv-2508-07805.creator: Yerin Hwang Dongryeol Lee, Taegwan Kang Yongil Kim Kyomin Jung
arxiv-2508-07805.description: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) take on growing roles as automated evaluators in practical settings, a critical question arises: Can individuals persuade an LLM judge to assign unfairly high scores? This study is the first to reveal that strategically embedded persuasive language can bias LLM judges when scoring mathematical reasoning tasks, where correctness should be independent of stylistic variation.

arxiv-2508-14355.title: D²-LIO: Enhanced Optimization for LiDAR-IMU Odometry Considering Directional Degeneracy
arxiv-2508-14355.creator: Guodong Yao, Hao Wang, Qing Chang
arxiv-2508-14355.description: Abstract LiDAR-inertial odometry (LIO) plays a vital role in achieving accurate localization and mapping, especially in complex environments. However, the presence of LiDAR feature degeneracy poses a major challenge to reliable state estimation. To overcome this issue, we propose an enhanced LIO framework that integrates adaptive outlier-tolerant correspondence with a scan-to-submap registration strategy.

arxiv-2509-21022.title: Actor-Critic without Actor
arxiv-2509-21022.creator: Donghyeon Ki, Hee-Jun Ahn, Kyungyoon Kim, Byung-Jun Lee
arxiv-2509-21022.description: Abstract Actor-critic methods constitute a central paradigm in reinforcement learning (RL), coupling policy evaluation with policy improvement. While effective across many domains, these methods rely on separate actor and critic networks, which makes training vulnerable to architectural decisions and hyperparameter tuning. Such complexity limits their scalability in settings that require large function approximators.

arxiv-2601-11516.title: Building Production-Ready Probes For Gemini
arxiv-2601-11516.creator: János Kramár, Joshua Engels, Zheng Wang, Bilal Chughtai, Rohin Shah, Neel Nanda, Arthur Conmy
arxiv-2601-11516.description: Abstract Frontier language model capabilities are improving rapidly. We thus need stronger mitigations against bad actors misusing increasingly powerful systems. Prior work has shown that activation probes may be a promising misuse mitigation technique, but we identify a key remaining challenge: probes fail to generalize under important production distribution shifts.

arxiv-2602-20256.title: Feng He,
arxiv-2602-20256.creator: Arthur Hutsalyuk,
arxiv-2602-20256.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Arthur Hutsalyuk,. Spectral Decimation of Quantum Many-Body Hamiltonians Abstract We develop a systematic theory of spectral decimation for quantum many-body Hamiltonians and show that it provides a quantitative probe of emergent symmetries in statistically mixed spectra. Building on an analytical description of statistical mixtures, we derive an explicit expression for the size of a characteristic symmetry sector (CSS), defined as the largest subsequence of levels exhibiting non-Poissonian correlations.

pmc-10544547.creator: Mohamad Mahjoor, Golnaz Mahmoudvand, Simin Farokhi, Alireza Shadab, Mojtaba Kashfi, Hamed Afkhami
pmc-10544547.description: The Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT) is an intricate signaling cascade composed of various cytokines, interferons (IFN, growth factors, and other molecules. This pathway provides a delicate mechanism through which extracellular factors adjust gene expression, thereby acting as a substantial basis for environmental signals to influence cell growth and differentiation.

pmc-10612156.title: Comparison of erector spinae plane block with paravertebral block for thoracoscopic surgery: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-10612156.creator: Jinghua Pang, Jiawen You, Yong Chen, Chengjun Song
pmc-10612156.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionThe efficacy of erector spinae plane block versus paravertebral block for thoracoscopic surgery remains controversial. We conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to explore the impact of erector spinae plane block versus paravertebral block on thoracoscopic surgery.MethodsWe have searched PubMed, EMbase, Web of science, EBSCO, and Cochrane library databases through March 2022 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing the effect of erector spinae plane block versus paravertebral block on thoracoscopic surgery.

pmc-10657249.title: Exploring the Factors That Influence Stakeholder Participation in Decision-Making for the Moat System Restoration Project in Tianchang City, China
pmc-10657249.creator: Shihua Yan, Roziya Binti Ibrahim
pmc-10657249.description: The driving factors have a critical effect on shaping stakeholder behavior toward participating in decision-making for river restoration initiatives. The participation of stakeholders is a vital determinant for increasing public confidence in the government and enhancing the acceptance of government decisions. Conversely, insufficient stakeholder participation in decision-making may lead to resistance to decisions on river restoration projects.

pmc-12433023.title: Association of stress hyperglycemia ratio with clinical outcomes in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus in intensive care units: a retrospective study
pmc-12433023.creator: Jinzhan Chen, Ayun Chen, Ning Zhang, Zhisheng Chen, Jinxian Huang, Hongni Jiang, Congyi Xie
pmc-12433023.description: BackgroundCo-morbidity of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) corresponds to increasing severity and adverse clinical outcomes. This study intends to investigate the association of stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) with adverse outcomes in critically ill patients with COPD and T2DM.

pmc-12507665.title: Rewiring of cortical glucose metabolism fuels human brain cancer growth
pmc-12507665.creator: Andrew J Scott, Anjali Mittal, Baharan Meghdadi, Alexandra O’Brien, Justine Bailleul, Palavalasa Sravya, Abhinav Achreja, Weihua Zhou, Jie Xu, Angelica Lin, Kari Wilder-Romans, Ningning Liang, Ayesha U Kothari, Navyateja Korimerla, Donna M Edwards, Zhe Wu, Jiane Feng, Sophia Su, Li Zhang, Peter Sajj
pmc-12507665.description: The brain avidly consumes glucose to fuel neurophysiology1. Cancers of the brain, such as glioblastoma, relinquish physiological integrity and gain the ability to proliferate and invade healthy tissue2. How brain cancers rewire glucose use to drive aggressive growth remains unclear.

Estrous synchronization is a tool that allows dairy operations to control the estrous cycle of the cow and facilitate timed insemination.

pmc-13354293.title: Anterior cingulate cortex monitors action state and action content in complex associative learning
pmc-13354293.creator: Wenqiang Huang, Arron F Hall, Natalia Kawalec, Ashley Nicole Opalka, Jun Liu, Dong V Wang, Alicia Izquierdo, Wenqiang Huang, Arron F Hall, Natalia Kawalec, Ashley Nicole Opalka, Jun Liu, Dong V Wang
pmc-13354293.description: Environmental changes necessitate adaptive responses, and thus the ability to monitor one’s actions and their connection to specific cues and outcomes is crucial for survival. The anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) is implicated in these processes, yet its precise role in action monitoring vs. outcome tracking remains unclear.

pmc-13443586.title: Association between loneliness trajectories and chronic diseases as well as chronic comorbidities among middle - aged and elderly chinese: based on the group - based trajectory modeling method
pmc-13443586.creator: Yihang Pang, Yongrong Jiang, Naiqian Sa, Ge Xu
pmc-13443586.description: This study aims to investigate the associations between loneliness trajectories and chronic diseases and chronic comorbidities among middle aged and elderly Chinese individuals. This study included 8,935 participants aged ≥ 45 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (2011–2020). Loneliness was assessed using a single item 4 point scale.

pmc-13527806.title: Factors Influencing the Choice of Surgery as a Future Career among Medical Students: A Cross-Sectional Multi-Institutional Study in Edo State, Nigeria
pmc-13527806.creator: Esteem Tagar, James Kpolugbo, Afokeoghene Gift Tagar, William Akerele, Lucky Aroboinosen Ehiagwina, Clement Osime, Ifeanyichukwu Michael Chukwu
pmc-13527806.description: Background:There are concerns in some countries regarding a decline in medical students' interest in pursuing surgery as a career. Our study aimed to assess interest in a surgical career and the factors influencing medical students' career choices.Methodology:We conducted a cross-sectional study involving medical students in the three clinical years at three medical schools in Edo State, southern Nigeria.

pmc-13632092.creator: Xiaoqian Chen, Ziyan Yue, Yifei Li, Weixi Yang, Shugang Li, Xiaobin Ma, Maurice O'Sullivan, Hong Zeng, Yanbo Wang
pmc-13632092.description: Preserved eggs (PEs) are a traditional Chinese pickled product known for the distinctive flavor. However, the formation mechanisms of such iconic flavor remain unclear. In this study, electronic nose (E-nose), gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS), gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS), and metabolomics analysis were performed to investigate the spatiotemporal flavor evolution of preserved eggs during pickling.
